'''Kylor Kelley''' (born August 26, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Converge FiberXers]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]].

==Early life==
Kelley grew up playing basketball under the coaching of his mother, a former high school player.<ref name="bennett">{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Bennett|title=Look, Mom, all smiles! Kylor Kelley works through severe dental issues to become Oregon State's top shot-blocker|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/798144/2019/02/04/look-mom-all-smiles-kylor-kelley-works-through-severe-dental-issues-to-become-oregon-states-top-shot-blocker/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=February 4, 2019|access-date=June 17, 2020}}</ref> At age six or seven, he moved with his mother and brother from Utah to Oregon after his parents split.<ref name="meek">{{cite web|first=Austin|last=Meek|title=Oregon State's Kylor Kelley took a winding road to OSU record book|url=https://www.registerguard.com/sports/20181224/austin-meek-oregon-states-kylor-kelley-took-winding-road-to-osu-record-book|work=[[The Register-Guard]]|date=December 24, 2018|access-date=June 17, 2020|archive-date=August 10, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200810061347/https://www.registerguard.com/sports/20181224/austin-meek-oregon-states-kylor-kelley-took-winding-road-to-osu-record-book|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kelley played three years of [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball for [[Gervais High School]] in [[Gervais, Oregon]].<ref name="sowa">{{cite web|first=Jesse|last=Sowa|title=OSU men's basketball: Kylor Kelley has left his mark as a shot-blocker|url=https://democratherald.com/sports/beavers-sports/basketball/osu-mens-basketball-kylor-kelley-has-left-his-mark-as-a-shot-blocker/article_80c2d281-150d-5be3-a5a2-01d1ce32427e.html|work=[[Albany Democrat-Herald]]|date=February 7, 2020|access-date=June 17, 2020}}</ref> While attending Gervais, he grew from 6'1 to 7'0 but did not weigh more than 185 pounds.<ref name="daschel">{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Daschel|title=For Oregon State 7-footer Kylor Kelley, it's now books before blocks|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/sports/g66l-2019/01/81c73d5b5d9615/for-oregon-state-7footer-kylor-kelley-its-now-books-before-blocks.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=January 23, 2019|access-date=June 17, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, Kelley averaged 15.9 points, 12.4 rebounds, 7.8 blocks, and 2.4 assists per game and was named PacWest Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web | last=Nemec | first=Andrew | title=Kylor Kelley, 7-foot-1 in-state transfer, commits to Oregon State Beavers men's basketball | website=oregonlive | date=2017-06-09 | url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2017/06/kylor_kelley_7-foot-1_in-state.html | access-date=2025-12-07}}</ref> He set the school's career, single-season and single-game records for blocks.<ref name="horowitz">{{cite web|first=Gary|last=Horowitz|title=Gervais product Kylor Kelley hopes to make impact at OSU|url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/college/oregon-state/2018/11/03/oregon-state-university-basketball-kylor-kelley-pac-12/1763351002/|work=[[Statesman Journal]]|date=November 3, 2018|access-date=June 17, 2020}}</ref> Kelley did not qualify to play for most four-year colleges. As a result, he had no [[NCAA Division I]] offers out of high school.<ref name=daschel/>

==College career==
Kelley began playing college basketball for [[Bushnell University|Northwest Christian University]]. As a freshman, Kelley averaged 8.6 points, 8.8 rebounds and 5.6 blocks per game and set a school single-game record with 10 blocks against [[Southern Oregon University|Southern Oregon]].<ref name="tucson">{{cite web|title=His story is a mouthful|url=https://tucson.com/his-story-is-a-mouthful/article_bba7a674-1bad-11e9-8c06-c3e9c57f5528.html|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=January 18, 2019|access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref> After 10 games, he was dismissed from Bushnell. Kelley transferred to [[Lane Community College]], where he received more Division I interest as a result. In his sophomore season, he averaged 9.9 points, 7.5 rebounds and 4.6 blocks per game and was a [[Northwest Athletic Conference]] All-Defensive Team selection.<ref name="santora">{{cite web|first=Mario|last=Santora|title=OSU basketball player Kylor Kelley credits LCC for his success on and off court|url=https://kval.com/sports/content/osu-basketball-player-kylor-kelley-credits-lcc-for-his-success-on-and-off-court|website=KVAL.com|publisher=[[KVAL-TV]]|date=January 29, 2020|access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref>

At Lane CC, Kelley was recruited by multiple [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] programs and chose to continue his career at [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] because he wanted to stay close to home.<ref name="akins">{{cite web|first=Brady|last=Akins|title=Oregon State's record-breaking underdog|url=http://www.orangemedianetwork.com/daily_barometer/oregon-states-record-breaking-underdog/article_eae88abe-5b2d-11ea-a384-f7ce42400587.html|work=Orange Media Network|date=March 2, 2020|access-date=June 21, 2020|archive-date=June 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200622192430/http://www.orangemedianetwork.com/daily_barometer/oregon-states-record-breaking-underdog/article_eae88abe-5b2d-11ea-a384-f7ce42400587.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 17, 2018, as a junior at Oregon State, Kelley tallied a school-record nine blocks, to go with 10 points and nine rebounds, in an 82–67 victory over [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Daschel|title=Kylor Kelley's record-setting night helps Oregon State roll Pepperdine 82–67: at a glance|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/sports/2018/12/live-updates-oregon-state-faces-pepperdine-as-it-tries-to-end-two-game-skid.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=December 17, 2018|access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref> By the end of the season, he ranked second in the nation, led the Pac-12 and set a school record with 3.35 blocks per game. He also averaged 7.7 points and five rebounds per game and was named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kylor Kelley shows no intention of slowing down after shattering Oregon State's blocks record|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/teens/2019/07/oregon-states-kylor-kelley-destroys-record-shows-no-intention-of-slowing-down.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|publisher=High School Journalism Institute|date=July 20, 2019|access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref> On December 18, 2019, as a senior, Kelley posted a season-high 23 points, six rebounds and three blocks in an 88–78 win over [[UTSA Roadrunners men's basketball|UTSA]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ethan Thompson, Kylor Kelley score 23 apiece as Oregon State men's basketball beats UTSA|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2019/12/ethan-thompson-kylor-kelley-score-23-apiece-as-oregon-state-mens-basketball-beats-utsa.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 18, 2019|access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref> He became Oregon State's all-time leader in blocks in a January 30, 2020, victory over [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], during which he posted 10 points, seven blocks and six rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kelley, Lucas Lead Beavers To Road Win Over Stanford|url=https://osubeavers.com/news/2020/1/31/mens-basketball-kelley-lucas-lead-beavers-to-road-win-over-stanford.aspx|work=Oregon State University Athletics|date=January 30, 2020|access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref> Kelley finished his senior season averaging 11.1 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.45 blocks per game, earning Pac-12 All-Defensive Team honors for a second time. He averaged the second-most blocks per game in the nation and led the Pac-12 in that category.<ref name="oregonstate">{{cite web|title=Kylor Kelley|url=https://osubeavers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kylor-kelley/7472|work=Oregon State University Athletics|access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref> Despite the Pac-12 Tournament being cancelled due to the coronavirus pandemic, Kelley finished with 211 blocks in two years at Oregon State.<ref>{{cite news|first=Orlando|last=Sanchez|title=Beavers big man Kylor Kelley poised for the next level|url=https://www.kgw.com/article/sports/beavers-big-man-poised-for-the-next-level/283-6910f791-e899-4f06-b5e1-5664d1668ea2|work=KGW8|date=May 4, 2020|access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Austin Spurs (2021)===
After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], on December 11, 2020, Kelley was reported to have signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] and subsequently waived by the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Suleymanov|title=Spurs Sign, Waive Kylor Kelley|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/12/spurs-sign-waive-kylor-kelley.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 11, 2020|access-date=December 12, 2020}}</ref> Kelley was included in the roster of [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs announce 2021 roster|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2021-roster|website=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2021|access-date=February 1, 2021}}</ref>

===London Lions (2021–2022)===
On July 21, 2021, Kelley signed with the [[London Lions (basketball)|London Lions]] for the [[2021–22 British Basketball League season|2021–22 BBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kylor Kelley confirmed to join London Lions for upcoming season|url=https://www.thelondonlions.com/news/408/|date=July 21, 2021|website=TheLondonLions.com|access-date=July 21, 2021|archive-date=July 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210721125313/https://www.thelondonlions.com/news/408/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lions add Kylor Kelley to pack|url=http://www.bbl.org.uk/lions-add-kylor-kelley-to-pack/|website=BBL.org.uk|date=July 21, 2021|access-date=July 21, 2021}}</ref>

===Bakken Bears (2022)===
On August 29, 2022, Kelley signed with [[Bakken Bears]] of the [[Basketball Champions League|Champions League]] and the Danish [[Basketligaen]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Sebastian|last=Pfaff|title=Bakken Bears opruster med endnu en amerikaner|url=https://fullcourt.dk/basketball-champions-league/bakken-bears-opruster-med-endnu-en-amerikaner/|website=FullCourt.dk|date=August 29, 2022|access-date=January 26, 2025|language=Danish}}</ref> However, he left the team on December 5, after 10 appearances.<ref>{{cite web|title=Samarbejdet med Kylor Kelley ophører|url=https://www.bakkenbears.com/2022/12/05/samarbejdet-med-kylor-kelley-ophoerer/|website=BakkenBears.com|date=December 5, 2022|access-date=January 26, 2025|language=Danish}}</ref>

===Raptors 905 (2023)===
On December 20, 2022, Kelley was reacquired by the [[Austin Spurs]], but was waived the next day without playing for the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=2022–2023 Austin Spurs Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Austin-Spurs/9/Transaction_History/2023|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 26, 2025}}</ref> On January 6, 2023, he was acquired by [[Raptors 905]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2022–2023 Raptors 905 Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Raptors-905/41/Transaction_History/2023|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 26, 2025}}</ref>

===Salem Capitals (2023)===
Kelley joined the [[Salem Capitals]] of [[The Basketball League]] (TBL) for the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kylor Kelley Game Log|url=https://hosted.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/TBBL/en/competition/35345/person/2014820/gamelog|website=geniussports.com|access-date=July 11, 2025}}</ref>

===Calgary Surge (2023)===
On May 12, 2023, Kelley signed with the [[Calgary Surge]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Calgary Surge Sign Kylor Kelley|url=https://www.cebl.ca/calgary-surge-sign-kylor-kelley|website=CEBL.ca|date=May 12, 2023|access-date=May 13, 2023}}</ref>

===Maine Celtics (2023–2024)===
On October 3, 2023, Kelley signed with the [[Boston Celtics]], but was waived the next day.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Celtics Sign, Waive Kylor Kelley|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/celtics-sign-kylor-kelley-to-exhibit-10-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 5, 2023|access-date=October 6, 2023}}</ref> On October 28, he joined the [[Maine Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maine Celtics Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-102823|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=October 28, 2023}}</ref>

===Return to Salem (2024)===
Kelley again joined the [[Salem Capitals]] for the 2024 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kylor Kelley Game Log|url=https://hosted.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/TBBL/en/competition/37917/person/2014820/gamelog|website=geniussports.com|access-date=July 11, 2025}}</ref>

===South Bay Lakers (2024–2025)===
On August 14, 2024, Kelley signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Kylor Kelley and Quincy Olivari|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-kylor-kelley-and-quincy-olivari-081424|website=NBA.com|date=August 14, 2024|access-date=August 14, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on October 18.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Grayson Murphy|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-grayson-murphy-101824|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}}</ref> On October 26, he joined the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Finalize Training Camp Roster and Schedule|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-finalize-training-camp-roster-and-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2025)===
On January 26, 2025, Kelley signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks announced today that they have signed center Kylor Kelley to a Two-Way contract and requested waivers on Two-Way guard Jazian Gortman. Kelley will wear No. 50 for the Mavericks.|number=1883658844515316024|user=MavsPR|date=January 26, 2025|access-date=January 26, 2025}}</ref> He made his NBA debut the next day against the [[Washington Wizards]], scoring one point and grabbing four rebounds in a blowout win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Klay Thompson makes 7 3s in 1st quarter as Mavs breeze past NBA-worst Wizards 130–108|url=https://www.nba.com/game/was-vs-dal-0022400657|website=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2025|access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref> Kelley was waived by Dallas on March 3.<ref>{{cite tweet|title=The Dallas Mavericks announced today that they have signed center Kai Jones to a Two-Way contract.|number=1896697131983098045|user=MavsPR|date=March 3, 2025|access-date=March 3, 2025}}</ref>

===Return to South Bay (2025)===
On March 8, 2025, the [[South Bay Lakers]] announced that Kelley had re-joined their roster.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=South Bay Lakers|title=OFFICIAL: Center Kylor Kelley has rejoined the South Bay Lakers roster.|number=1898449280609993016|user=southbaylakers|date=March 8, 2025|access-date=March 8, 2025}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2025)===
On April 3, 2025, the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] announced that they had signed Kelley to 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Kylor Kelley to 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/kylor-kelley-center-10-day-contract-pelicans-roster-april-3-2025|date=April 3, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 3, 2025}}</ref> On April 13, Kelley re-signed with the Pelicans for the final game of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pelicans Sign Kylor Kelley|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/pelicans-sign-kylor-kelley|access-date=May 14, 2025|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Pallacanestro Trieste (2025)===
On May 7, 2025, he signed with [[Pallacanestro Trieste]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pallacanestrotrieste.it/la-pallacanestro-trieste-punta-in-alto-ingaggiato-il-lungo-nba-kylor-kelley/|title=La Pallacanestro Trieste Punta in Alto, Ingaggiato Il Lungo NBA Kylor Kelley|last=|first=|date=May 7, 2025|website=pallacanestrotrieste.it|publisher=|language=it|access-date=May 7, 2025}}</ref>

===Third stint with South Bay (2025–2026)===
On August 25, 2025, Kelley signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Center Kylor Kelley|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-center-kylor-kelley-082525|website=NBA.com|date=August 25, 2025|access-date=August 29, 2025}}</ref> He got waived by Los Angeles on September 28.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-29 |title=Kylor Kelley: Waived by Los Angeles |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kylor-kelley-waived-by-los-angeles/ |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> Kelley subsequently re-joined the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite news|title= South Bay Lakers Announce Training Camp Roster |url= https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-announce-training-camp-roster |access-date=November 2, 2025 |work=[[NBA G League]] |date=October 29, 2025}}</ref>

===Converge FiberXers (2026)===
On February 18, 2026, it was reported that the [[Converge FiberXers]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) has tapped the services of Kelley as its import in the upcoming [[2026 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Justine |last=Bacnis |url=https://tiebreakertimes.com.ph/tbt/converge-bolsters-frontline-with-kylor-kelley/365165 |title=Converge bolsters frontline with Kylor Kelley |website=Tiebreaker Times |date=February 18, 2026 |access-date=February 19, 2026 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kelley's father, Jeff, played college basketball for [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]]. His mother, Shandel Howell, had intended to play the same sport for [[Utah State Aggies women's basketball|Utah State]] before its women's program was cut by the university.<ref name=daschel/>
